environment_fingerprint: windows-11-26200-x64-dotnet-sdk-10.0.400-pwsh7-windows-app-runtime-1.7; dotnet-only host without Visual Studio Appx packaging tasks
commands: pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/build-preview.ps1 -Target WinUICompat (after temporarily removing EnableCoreMrtTooling=false)

coverage: At base commit d2ccb55 the Compatibility Preview builds with zero warnings/errors and passes the bounded launch smoke while Core MRT tooling remains disabled.
The output directory contains no .pri: theme/control resources resolve through the existing fail-soft TryGetValue resolver, so missing resources render unstyled instead of crashing.
The historical 0xC000027B startup crash was fixed by the fail-soft resolver (#548 / PR #571), not by keeping Core MRT tooling enabled.

results.command: build-preview.ps1 -Target WinUICompat with EnableCoreMrtTooling=false temporarily removed
coverage: The dotnet-only build fails immediately with MSB4062: MrtCore.PriGen requires Microsoft.Build.AppxPackage tasks that exist only with Visual Studio on this host.
Keeping Core MRT tooling disabled is required for the documented dotnet-only Compatibility Preview path; the project change was reverted after reproduction.

corrections: PR #694 and evidence/0000-foundation/compat-preview-build-v1.json state that Compatibility Preview keeps Core MRT resource tooling enabled and that this fixes the startup crash. Commit bcedc4a actually only added a UTF-8 BOM to Hibiki.WinUI.csproj; the disable flag remains present and the launch fix predates this slice (#548).

Truthful boundary: Compatibility Preview keeps Core MRT tooling disabled, emits no PRI, launches unstyled via the fail-soft resolver, and its build/launch smoke is not styling, resource-loading, accessibility or formal XAML evidence.
limitations: Reproduction covers this dotnet-only Windows host; VS2026-class hosts may behave differently and remain outside this audit.

After reverting the experimental change, the first incremental smoke runs crashed because the failed PRI build left mixed artifacts; moving the output directory aside and rebuilding produced a passing smoke. A post-failure WinUICompat smoke must use a clean output directory.
No runtime behavior, formal XAML, accessibility or audio/driver capability is claimed.
